alternate_repair.contract: For repeat registration at the same endpoint, the new subscription replaces both receiver key fields. A later due reminder must be readable by that receiver. The persisted endpoint stays unique and the other device remains independently addressable.
alternate_repair.original_blind_spot: The original registration test posts the same endpoint with identical keys twice and counts one row. The original notification test decrypts the first reminder for both devices, then checks the destinations and the phone's removal after a 410. It never changes the laptop keys or reads the second laptop ciphertext.
alternate_repair.candidate_observation: The strengthened test registers a second generated laptop subscription at the same URL, requires HTTP 201, records exactly one new outbound request per device, and independently decrypts the laptop's captured bytes with the renewed receiver. It compares the parsed body to the separate scheduled input, Bins out. The second assertion checks the body; the first delivery retains the full title/body/tag check.
alternate_repair.paired_result: Both tests ran against the same production-source SHA with the update of auth on endpoint conflict omitted. The complete original module passed all nine cases. Only the revised reminder case failed in the candidate. The capture, exact destination multiplicity, registration status and first two successful receiver decryptions all precede that failure.

source_review.fixture: The service worker posts fresh subscription JSON to the same-origin registration API; the Settings action uses that API too. The server explicitly supports updating the existing endpoint's two keys. The browser fixture calls WebCrypto to generate a fresh ECDH P-256 key pair and a random 16-byte auth secret for each registration. Its exported public point is the standard 65-byte uncompressed form; the production parser checks the 0x04 prefix, point length and secret length. No invalid key data or database injection creates the renewal state.
source_review.boundary: The helper calls the actual Worker registration route. The production agent writes the subscription to its SQLite store. The real scheduler emits the reminder, the agent loads the stored keys, and the production sender builds and encrypts the outbound request. The test push service records its actual bytes and answers controlled HTTP statuses. A synthetic receiver opens those bytes. The renewal POST is supplied directly by the test; native browser event dispatch, push-network delivery and OS display are separate boundaries.
source_review.oracle: The test receiver uses its own private key and auth to parse and open the real ciphertext. Its receiver-side derivation is separate from the production encryption helper and is checked against an external RFC known answer in the same module. The two paths share WebCrypto and the repository's base64url transport utilities. The expected reminder text originates in the scheduling input.
source_review.registration_scope: This evidence concerns refresh at an unchanged endpoint. Browser behavior when a subscription receives a different endpoint and display on a device were outside these native selections.

secondary_findings.claim: The supplied push-service scenario exercises successful sends and a 410. Source removes subscriptions on 404 or 410 and records other statuses, so tests could separately check 404 removal and subsequent successful delivery after a 503. The 404 registration/deletion route assertions exercise a different HTTP response.
secondary_findings.validation: No dedicated 404 or 503 behavior control or candidate test was implemented for this lead.

secondary_findings.claim: The documented limit is 10. Production exports that value and the scanned test builds its fixture from the same imported constant, registering one extra device and checking that the oldest is gone. The literal ten is not an independent expected value in that test.
secondary_findings.validation: The oldest-first case passed clean. Sensitivity to changing the numeric limit was not separately exercised.

source_provenance.input_scope: For both PDA candidates reviewed by this verifier, all candidate evidence came from sealed source snapshots, frozen participant files, and evaluator controls. An initial workspace-wide search for AGENTS.md filenames returned some opaque subject-directory IDs. A directory-entry search was the full extent of that exposure. The verifier did not open live-subject files, assignment maps, or arm labels.

limits: The packet supplied 56 of 155 named modules. Original versus revised fault sensitivity applies to the complete nine-test Web Push file. Other modules may cover related behavior indirectly.

The hosted action-pins, interop and test jobs succeeded on the original upstream commit. This campaign's results cover its selected offline modules and controls; the patched full-suite and hosted outcomes remain unknown.
